beats.title: 01 — Start with one neuron
beats.text: How can simple arithmetic help read a medical scan? Start with one artificial neuron.

beats.title: 02 — A small calculation
beats.text: It multiplies inputs by weights, adds a bias, then applies an activation. Here, two weighted inputs produce one output.

beats.title: 03 — Why activation matters
beats.text: Nonlinear activations matter. Without them, stacked layers collapse into a single weighted sum plus bias.

beats.title: 04 — Neurons become a layer
beats.text: Put neurons side by side. Each has its own weights, so the same inputs produce different responses. That's a layer.

beats.title: 05 — Layers become a network
beats.text: Feed those outputs into another layer, then another. Now you have one neural network: a chain of transformations.

beats.title: 06 — Training makes it useful
beats.text: During training, prediction errors adjust weights and biases. More neurons alone don't make the network useful.

beats.title: 07 — From patterns to medicine
beats.text: Large networks can learn complex image patterns. A validated medical imaging model can flag suspicious regions for clinicians to review.

beats.title: 08 — The complete picture
beats.text: Many neurons. Multiple layers. One trained network supporting a real task.
